data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network of small services is more resilient to correlated failure if and only if the diversity of their operational substrates (OS, hardware, cloud provider) exceeds the redundancy depth of the monolithic alternative.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services all rely on a single shared global dependency (e.g., AWS Route 53).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The monolithic service employs truly heterogeneous redundancy (e.g., multi-architecture, multi-region, multi-cloud) that exceeds the diversity of the decentralized network.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The failure mode of a monolithic service is bounded by its shared kernel or global state; conversely, a decentralized network's failure is bounded by the intersection of its operators' common dependencies (e.g., a shared DNS provider or a common library version). Resilience is achieved by minimizing this intersection area.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
